reason: The original immutable-intent and unknown-ownership rules also apply to competing command controllers and failed startup calls. These additional checks are frozen before implementation and execution.

cases.expected: Intent identity and immutable data have a verified MAC across restart. Changed data or an unsigned legacy intent refuses authority and remains unresolved; migration retains original records.

Independent command controllers serialize the same runner slot. A crashed controller's durable unresolved intent prevents another launch even after its OS lock is released; only complete owned stop observations permit later admission.

A native Claude startup frame followed by a failed or limited initialization turn cannot grant a work lease. The actual failed call remains recorded, and overlapping model turns on one owned host refuse.

scope: Runtime invocation ownership only; task policy and protected merge commands remain unchanged.
